purpose: Provide a complete, human-readable trust and audit trail for Isabel conclusions, recommendations, approvals, executions, and verification.
principles: Every consequential conclusion must retain its supporting evidence references and confidence.
Inference must be visibly distinguishable from confirmed fact.
Every approval must identify the exact payload, approver, timestamp, and scope.
Every executed action must record what actually happened, not merely what was planned.
Verification must be a separate event from execution.
Corrections append a superseding record; prior records are not silently rewritten.
User-facing summaries remain concise while the full chain stays inspectable.
acceptance_tests: A recommendation can be traced back to every supporting source.
A consequential action cannot show as approved without an approval record tied to an exact payload hash.
Execution success and verification success are stored separately.
If evidence is corrected, the old record remains visible and the replacement points back to it.
A reviewer can reconstruct the entire decision chain without relying on chat history.
